content1.content: 📘 Basics of Custom Widgets in Flutter

content2.content: Flutter is known for its flexible widget system. In Flutter, everything is a widget, and learning how to create custom widgets is essential to build clean, reusable, and scalable apps.

content4.content: Custom widgets are user-defined widgets that combine one or more built-in widgets. They allow you to:

content5.content:
Reuse UI components across screens
Organize your code better
Make your code cleaner and easier to maintain

content9.content:
Avoid repetition
Separate UI into meaningful pieces
Increase code reusability
Improve readability and debugging

content12.content: Flutter provides two main types of widgets you can extend:

row2: UI that does not change over time
row3: UI that can change (has internal state)

content32.content: Custom widgets can accept parameters like any class:

content36.content:
Use meaningful names (UserCard, ProductTile, etc.)
Make widgets small and focusedUse const where possible for performance

Extract widgets as separate files if they grow large

content38.content:
Custom widgets help organize your UI
Use StatelessWidget for static content
Use StatefulWidget for dynamic content
Pass data using constructor parameters
